title: Error-state phrasing and live-region patterns — a11y grooming
summary: Working notes and proposed patterns for consistent, accessible error messaging across console components. Focus areas: concise phrasing, error severity taxonomy, live-region usage for dynamic errors, recovery affordances, and wireframe annotations for error placement.
body:
Context:
- Aim: reduce user confusion when operations fail (create model, upload file, route config) and ensure screen reader users receive timely, non-redundant, and actionable feedback.
- Current issues observed in usability tests: inconsistent phrasing, live regions not present for inline validation, duplicate announcements (toast + inline), and missing guidance for recovery.

Key principles (proposal):
1) Prioritize explicitness and actionability: error copy should state what failed, why (brief), and the next step. E.g. 'Upload failed: file exceeded 250 MB. Resize or split the file and try again.'
2) Use a clear severity taxonomy across components:
   - inline-field-error (low, persistent near control)
   - toast-alert (medium, ephemeral, global)
   - blocking-modal-error (high, requires acknowledgement)
3) Single-source announcement for the same problem: pick either the inline element or the toast to announce, not both. If both are shown, only toast should be aria-live polite and inline should be aria-hidden for SRs to avoid duplicate reads.
4) Avoid jargon; keep lines <= 100 characters for readability and SR pauses.

ARIA and live-region patterns:
- Inline form validation (on blur or submit): use role="status" and aria-live="polite" on the inline container when the message appears. Ensure the element receives focus only when a corrective action is requested (do not shift focus for non-blocking errors).
- Toasts for background ops (save, deploy): toasts should use aria-live="assertive" for deployment failures that require immediate attention. For transient warnings, use polite.
- Modal/blocking errors: focus trap into modal, set role="alertdialog" and provide an explicit close/acknowledge button with clear label. Screen reader should hear the modal title + short error copy.
- Prevent double reads: a single aria-live region per page for toasts, and inline messages must not duplicate toasts. Implementation detail: toasts inject into #console-toast-live (aria-live region). Inline error containers have data-sr-announced="false" by default; JS toggles to true only when inline is the primary communicator.

Error-copy variants (examples to A/B test):
- Create model failure (network):
  A: 'Model creation failed due to a network timeout. Check your connection and try again.'
  B: 'We couldn’t create the model because the network timed out. Retry or view logs for details.'
- Upload size error:
  A: 'Upload failed. File > 250 MB. Compress or split and re-upload.'
  B: 'File too large. Maximum allowed is 250 MB. Use a smaller file.'
- Permission denied (background job):
  A: 'Action blocked: you need the "Deploy models" permission. Contact an admin.'
  B: 'Permission required: ask an admin to grant Deploy models access.'

Wireframe annotations (component-level):
- Inline input with helper text: reserve 1 line under the input for helper/error. When error appears, helper text fades out to preserve layout. Error icon placed left of text, color from semantic token --error-500. Screen reader order: input -> aria-describedby -> error message.
- Global toast: top-right anchored. Provide a visible 'View details' link for errors that have logs or retry actions. For SR: toast title announced first, then concise body.
- Console-wide banner (for region or service outages): full-width, role="region" and aria-label="Platform status". Banner must include a short status summary and link to status page.

Accessibility testing checklist (manual + automated):
- NVDA/VoiceOver: verify single announcement per failure flow, modals receive focus, toasts do not steal input focus.
- Keyboard: ensure error actions (retry, view logs, contact support) are reachable and in logical tab order.
- Contrast: error text and icons must meet AA contrast against background in both light/dark themes.
- Reduced-motion: any error animation (shake, flash) should respect prefers-reduced-motion and provide a non-animated emphasis alternative.
- Screen reader verbosity: avoid verbose diagnostics for SRs; surface link to detailed logs rather than the full stack trace.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- New helper utilities: create an error-surface component with props {severity, announceMode} where announceMode: 'inline' | 'toast' | 'modal'. Component maps to ARIA roles and CSS tokens.
- Centralize toast live region to /src/ui/toast/ToastLiveRegion.tsx and prevent duplication by de-duping keys for identical errors.
- Create unit tests that simulate repeated errors and ensure the live region text updates (and that duplicate text is not repeated verbatim to avoid SR repetitive reads).

Backlog grooming (actionable tickets):
- CON-2147: Implement error-surface component with announceMode API (owner: Marco).
- CON-2148: Migrate upload flow to use error-surface and ensure only toast used for background upload failures (owner: Devon).
- CON-2149: Update modal error pattern to use role=alertdialog and add acceptance tests (owner: Sofia).
- CON-2150: Copy A/B experiment for 'Model creation failed' messages (owner: Aisha).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default preference for assertive vs polite for mid-severity toasts? Recommendation: assertive for failures that affect ability to continue (deploys, saves), polite for recoverable warnings.
- Do we add an account-level setting to suppress non-critical live announcements for power users? Proposal: queue for later (post-launch).

Next steps for team sync (proposed agenda for 2026-07-14):
- Walk through wireframes and error-surface props (10 min)
- Accessibility demo: voiceover playback of flows (10 min)
- Assign implementation owners for CON tickets (10 min)
- Quick decision on assertive/polite defaults (5 min)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally focused on phrasing and announcement patterns rather than visual polish. We will coordinate with DS token owners for color/contrast but want copy/ARIA agreement first.
- Please comment on the A/B variants and severity mapping. If you have prior research links (e.g., existing SR test transcripts), paste into linked_artifacts.

Draft history: initial draft 2026-07-10 by Aisha Patel, updated with engineering feasibility notes 2026-07-12 by Marco Liu.
